sections.heading: Efficacy and safety versus warfarin in atrial fibrillation

claims.text: In the RE-LY noninferiority trial, 18,113 patients with atrial fibrillation and a risk of stroke were randomly assigned to fixed doses of dabigatran 110 mg or 150 mg twice daily or to adjusted-dose warfarin, with a median follow-up of 2.0 years.

evidence.quote: In this noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned 18,113 patients who had atrial fibrillation and a risk of stroke to receive, in a blinded fashion, fixed doses of dabigatran--110 mg or 150 mg twice daily--or, in an unblinded fashion, adjusted-dose warfarin. The median duration of the follow-up period was 2.0 years.

claims.text: The rate of stroke or systemic embolism was 1.69% per year with warfarin, 1.53% per year with dabigatran 110 mg (relative risk 0.91; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority) and 1.11% per year with dabigatran 150 mg (relative risk 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82; P<0.001 for superiority).

evidence.quote: Rates of the primary outcome were 1.69% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 1.53% per year in the group that received 110 mg of dabigatran (relative risk with dabigatran, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority) and 1.11% per year in the group that received 150 mg of dabigatran (relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82; P<0.001 for superiority).

claims.text: Major bleeding occurred at 3.36% per year with warfarin, 2.71% per year with dabigatran 110 mg (P=0.003) and 3.11% per year with dabigatran 150 mg (P=0.31).

evidence.quote: The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P=0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.31).

claims.text: Hemorrhagic stroke occurred at 0.38% per year with warfarin versus 0.12% per year with dabigatran 110 mg (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with dabigatran 150 mg (P<0.001).

evidence.quote: The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.38% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 0.12% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001).

claims.text: Mortality was 4.13% per year with warfarin, 3.75% per year with dabigatran 110 mg (P=0.13) and 3.64% per year with dabigatran 150 mg (P=0.051).

evidence.quote: The mortality rate was 4.13% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 3.75% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P=0.13) and 3.64% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.051).

claims.text: In patients with atrial fibrillation, dabigatran 110 mg was associated with rates of stroke and systemic embolism similar to warfarin and lower rates of major hemorrhage, whereas dabigatran 150 mg was associated with lower rates of stroke and systemic embolism but similar rates of major hemorrhage.

evidence.quote: In patients with atrial fibrillation, dabigatran given at a dose of 110 mg was associated with rates of stroke and systemic embolism that were similar to those associated with warfarin, as well as lower rates of major hemorrhage. Dabigatran administered at a dose of 150 mg, as compared with warfarin, was associated with lower rates of stroke and systemic embolism but similar rates of major hemorrhage.

sections.heading: Efficacy and safety versus warfarin (ROCKET AF)

claims.text: In the double-blind ROCKET AF trial, 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation at increased risk for stroke were randomly assigned to rivaroxaban 20 mg daily or dose-adjusted warfarin.

evidence.quote: In a double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who were at increased risk for stroke to receive either rivaroxaban (at a daily dose of 20 mg) or dose-adjusted warfarin.

claims.text: In the per-protocol, as-treated primary analysis, the primary end point of stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 188 rivaroxaban patients (1.7% per year) and 241 warfarin patients (2.2% per year) (hazard ratio 0.79; 95% CI, 0.66 to 0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority).

claims.text: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary end point occurred in 269 rivaroxaban patients (2.1% per year) and 306 warfarin patients (2.4% per year) (hazard ratio 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority).

evidence.quote: In the intention-to-treat analysis, the primary end point occurred in 269 patients in the rivaroxaban group (2.1% per year) and 306 patients in the warfarin group (2.4% per year) (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority).

sections.heading: Japan-specific dose in Japanese patients (J-ROCKET AF)

claims.text: J-ROCKET AF was a prospective, randomized, double-blind, phase III trial in which 1,280 patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation at increased risk for stroke were randomized to rivaroxaban 15 mg once daily or warfarin dose-adjusted according to Japanese guidelines.

evidence.quote: J-ROCKET AF was a prospective, randomized, double-blind, phase III trial. Patients (n=1,280) with non-valvular AF at increased risk for stroke were randomized to receive 15 mg once-daily rivaroxaban or warfarin dose-adjusted according to Japanese guidelines.

claims.text: Non-inferiority of rivaroxaban to warfarin was confirmed for the principal safety outcome of major and non-major clinically relevant bleeding, which occurred at 18.04% per year with rivaroxaban and 16.42% per year with warfarin (hazard ratio 1.11; 95% CI, 0.87-1.42; P<0.001 for non-inferiority).

claims.text: Intracranial hemorrhage rates were 0.8% with rivaroxaban and 1.6% with warfarin, and there was a strong trend for a reduction in stroke/systemic embolism with rivaroxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio 0.49; P=0.050).

evidence.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we compared apixaban (at a dose of 5 mg twice daily) with warfarin (target international normalized ratio, 2.0 to 3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke.

claims.text: A prespecified meta-analysis pooled all 71,683 participants of the phase 3 randomised trials RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48, of whom 42,411 received a new oral anticoagulant and 29,272 received warfarin.

sections.heading: Very elderly patients unsuitable for standard doses

claims.text: J-ROCKET AF compared a Japan-specific rivaroxaban dose of 15 mg once daily with warfarin dose-adjusted according to Japanese guidelines in Japanese patients with atrial fibrillation, and demonstrated the safety of that Japan-specific dose.

evidence.quote: A separate trial, J-ROCKET AF, compared the safety of a Japan-specific rivaroxaban dose with warfarin administered according to Japanese guidelines in Japanese patients with AF.
J-ROCKET AF demonstrated the safety of a Japan-specific rivaroxaban dose and supports bridging the global ROCKET AF results into Japanese clinical practice.

lint.note: Dabigatran 150 mg twice daily was superior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism (RR 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82), whereas low-dose edoxaban was noninferior but not superior (HR 1.07; 97.5% CI, 0.87 to 1.31), and the meta-analysis found low-dose regimens gave no overall reduction in stroke or systemic embolic events (1.03, 0.84-1.27) with more ischaemic strokes (1.28, 1.02-1.60). The difference may be explained by dose and regimen rather than by agent.

In ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 both edoxaban regimens were noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism, but in ELDERCARE-AF a 15-mg once-daily dose was compared with placebo, not warfarin, in very elderly Japanese patients unsuitable for standard doses; the two results rest on different comparators and populations.

The documents describe warfarin's limitations and its use as comparator but give no target INR range except the 2.0 to 3.0 used in ARISTOTLE, and no data on time in therapeutic range outside ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48.
